Update (US Eastern Time 6:18 PM): Apple has also officially rolled out the public Release Candidate (RC) versions of macOS Tahoe 26.7 and macOS Sequoia 15.8, with build numbers matching those of the developer RCs listed below.

In addition to the macOS 27 developer beta 6, Apple has also simultaneously released the first RC of macOS Tahoe 26.7 and macOS Sequoia 15.8. Details are as follows.

Apple accelerates its macOS release pace

Last week, Apple rolled out the first beta of macOS 26.6.2, while also releasing the initial betas of iOS 26.6.1 and its counterparts.

The reason for the version number discrepancy is that Apple had already pushed out macOS 26.6.1 just a few days prior, along with macOS Sonoma 14.8.9 and macOS Sequoia 15.7.9, to patch a serious Screen Sharing vulnerability.

Today, in addition to officially releasing macOS 26.6.2, Apple also simultaneously launched the Release Candidate (RC) of macOS Tahoe 26.7 (25G220) and macOS Sequoia 15.8 (24H16).

The release notes only describe macOS Sequoia 15.8 as containing "important security fixes and is recommended for all users," while macOS Tahoe 26.7 is described as delivering "security fixes for your Mac."

Although neither update discloses specific details, both further reflect that Apple is accelerating its macOS release cycle in order to patch vulnerabilities uncovered through AI-powered tools.

For macOS Tahoe users, this RC is not expected to introduce new features, as Apple's focus has now shifted to macOS 27 Golden Gate and its beta phase, in a push to launch officially in just a few weeks.

That said, we are continuing to test both systems and will report back should we find anything noteworthy.

Have you discovered anything new in the macOS Tahoe 26.7 and macOS Sequoia 15.8 RCs? Let us know in the comments.
